title: Withheld Carry-Over on Catalog Orders from the OTC Allowance
content:
**Pharmacy Benefit, over-the-counter allowance — ledger rule.** Part or all of the carry-over from the latest forfeited quarter may be withheld from what a mail catalog order may use: the withheld carry-over is subtracted from the allowance balance first, before anything else is taken from it.

**Carry-over.** The carry-over is the amount loaded for the latest forfeited quarter less its purchases and less its forfeiture entry, never below zero. The latest forfeited quarter is the benefit quarter of the most recently posted forfeiture entry in the coverage's allowance activity.

**Rule.** The withheld carry-over is the whole carry-over where at least one retail receipt tagged to the current quarter carries a posting date and two or more mail catalog or online orders are still open to the member in the current quarter; one half (0.5) of the carry-over where at least one such receipt carries a posting date and fewer than two such orders are still open; and nothing where no retail receipt tagged to the current quarter carries a posting date.

**Terms used.** The current quarter is the calendar quarter that contains today. The orders still open are the plan's mail catalog and online orders allowed per quarter less those already tagged to the current quarter.

### Truth table

| Retail receipt of the current quarter with a posting date | Mail catalog or online orders still open | Withheld carry-over |
|---|---|---|
| At least one | Two or more | The whole carry-over |
| At least one | Fewer than two | One half of the carry-over |
| None | any | Nothing |

### Worked figures (hypothetical)

Latest forfeited quarter: $50.00 loaded, $30.00 of purchases, a forfeiture entry of $14.00. Carry-over: $50.00 less $30.00 less $14.00, that is $6.00.

- One posted retail receipt this quarter, 2 orders still open: $6.00 withheld.
- One posted retail receipt this quarter, 1 order still open: $3.00 withheld.
- No posted retail receipt this quarter: nothing withheld.
